reconcile.note: Fausset and colleagues confine Ecclesiastes' grief to speculative inquiry into the world's crookedness, not to wisdom itself, the sense Proverbs praises.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Does wisdom make people happy?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/wisdom_happy.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: Happy is the man who finds wisdom, The man who gets understanding.
sides.verseText: Happy is the man who finds wisdom, The man who gets understanding.

sides.snippet: For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
sides.verseText: For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
